0.1.0.title: The first yapmod release
0.1.0.summary: yapmod is a modded desktop client for Yapper. This first release focuses on the basics: a real desktop window, a proper titlebar, and a place to grow from.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Yapper now runs in its own desktop window.
Added a custom macOS titlebar overlay.
Introduced the yapmod logo and desktop icons.

0.1.1.title: Modals and configuration
0.1.1.summary: This release adds the building blocks for customizing yapmod and showing dialogs over the Yapper interface.

sections.heading: New
items: Added a reusable modal API for injected scripts.
Added a welcome modal shown on the first launch.
Added a config file with options for the native titlebar and starting maximized.

0.1.2.title: A smoother first launch
0.1.2.summary: A small release focused on fixing rough edges and making the app easier to install and use.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: macOS builds are now ad-hoc signed, so the app opens without a damaged app warning.
The login screen now opens when you are not signed in.
Improved the README and release workflow.

sections.heading: New
items: Release notes now appear after an update, so you can see what changed.
The version you last ran is saved in your config file.

0.2.0.title: Settings, links, and a website
0.2.0.summary: This release puts yapmod's options where you expect them: inside Yapper's own settings page. It also adds an official website with direct downloads and makes external links open in your normal browser.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Added a Yapmod section to Yapper's settings, so desktop options live next to the rest of the app.
Added an official landing page with direct download links for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
External links now open in your default browser instead of inside the app.

sections.heading: New
items: The native titlebar and start-maximized options can now be toggled from the settings page, and apply on the next launch.
Settings are stored in your config file and can be written to from the injected page.
The release notes modal now shows the version, release date, and changelog of every past release.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Following a link to another site no longer opens a broken window inside the desktop client.

0.3.1.title: Notifications that arrive
0.3.1.summary: This release makes the desktop notifications and the unread badge work on every platform.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Desktop notifications now show up in the notification center of your system. The webview cannot post them by itself, so yapmod hands them over to the system.
The number of unread messages now reaches the app icon, on the Dock, the taskbar and the panel.

sections.heading: New
items: Added a Desktop notifications option and a Show the unread badge option to the yapmod section in the settings.
Clicking a notification brings yapmod to the front and opens the message it was about.

sections.heading: How it works
items: Yapper keeps deciding when to notify you: muted channels and servers, Do Not Disturb, and a window that is in front are all respected.

0.3.0.title: Notifications, voice calls, and updates
0.3.0.summary: This release adds notification and mention badges on every platform, fixes voice calls on macOS, and makes yapmod easier to keep up to date.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Unread and mention badges now show up on servers and channels, with desktop notifications and notification sounds on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Voice calls now work on macOS. The first time you join a call, allow microphone access and your mic is live.
yapmod now checks for updates and shows a notice when a newer version is available.

sections.heading: New
items: Added a changelog in settings, so you can read the notes for every release from inside the app.
Added a documentation site with full-text search for setup, troubleshooting, FAQ and developer docs.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: The previous settings panel no longer stays visible when you switch sections.
Settings from older yapmod versions are migrated correctly, so your window options survive an update.
The Linux app now uses the proper Tux icon.

sections.heading: If your mic still does not work
items: Enable yapmod in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, then relaunch.
If yapmod is not listed there, run tccutil reset Microphone io.ilyeshdz.yapmod in Terminal and relaunch the app.

0.4.0.title: Themes and system tray
0.4.0.summary: This release adds system tray support, allowing yapmod to keep running in the background, and introduces custom theme support directly in the application.

sections.heading: Highlights
items: Added system tray support, allowing yapmod to keep running in the background when its window is closed.
Introduced custom theme support, with themes loaded from dedicated folders containing a CSS file and a manifest.json file.

sections.heading: New
items: yapmod can now remain active in the background, allowing desktop notifications to continue working while the window is hidden.
Custom themes can now be loaded directly into the application. The theme format and requirements are documented in the documentation site.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Fixed AppImage compatibility on newer Linux distributions by excluding bundled Wayland and display libraries, preventing crashes on Wayland sessions.
